fields.meaning: And, together with… (formal written language: 及び)
examples: The president and the department managers will attend the meeting.
Please fill in your name and address.
Eating, drinking and smoking are prohibited inside the building.

fields.meaning: Fortunately…, luckily… (幸いなことに)
fields.connection: 幸いなことに 幸い + [sentence/clause]
examples: Fortunately, not a single person was injured.
Fortunately, we were blessed with good weather throughout the trip.
Luckily, I made the last train.

fields.meaning: Gradually… (次第に)
examples: The sky has gradually grown brighter.
The pain gradually went away.
I have gradually gotten used to my new life, too.

fields.meaning: Even so…, even taking that into account… (それにしても)
examples: They said they'd be late, but even so, this is far too late.
Anyway, it's really hot today, isn't it?
I'd heard it was a difficult exam, but even so, I never expected it to be this hard.

fields.meaning: If you do that…, in that case… (そうすると)
examples: Please press this button. When you do, the ticket will come out.
I tried walking for 30 minutes every day. As a result, I started feeling better.

A: We leave at 6 a.m.
B: In that case, we'll have to get up at 5, won't we?

fields.meaning: At least…, at a minimum… (少なくとも)
examples: It will take at least a month to complete.
I, at least, believe him.
There were at least 100 participants.

fields.meaning: Immediately, at once… (直ちに)
examples: In case of fire, please evacuate immediately.
As soon as a problem is found, I will report it immediately.
The factory immediately stopped production.

fields.meaning: Do… (command from a superior, male speech in spoken language: たまえ)
examples: Come now, have a seat.
Don't hold back, say it.
You come along with us too.

fields.meaning: If you keep… (it will lead to a bad result: ていては)
examples: If you go out and play every night, you won't pass the exam.
If you're afraid of failure, you can't do anything.
If you keep spending money like that, you won't be able to save any.

fields.meaning: Repeatedly… and… (repeated over and over: ては)
examples: It was a life of eating and sleeping, eating and sleeping.
Writing and erasing, writing and erasing, I finally finished the letter.
The waves keep rolling in and drawing back.

fields.meaning: At the same time as…, simultaneous with… (と同時に)
fields.connection: V plain form + と同時に / N・Naである + と同時に
examples: The moment the door opened, the customers came in.
He is a student and, at the same time, a business owner.
The exam began the moment the bell rang.

fields.meaning: In such a way as…, in the manner of… (というふうに)
fields.connection: [sentence/clause] + という風に というふうに
examples: I've set my schedule like this: cleaning on Mondays, laundry on Tuesdays, and so on.
If you say something like 「体調が悪い」, you can take the day off.
They changed the rules so that anyone can take part.

fields.meaning: I hear that…, apparently because… (とかで)
fields.connection: V plain form + とか(で) / N + だ / Na + だ / Aい
examples: He went home early, apparently because he had something to do.
The trains have stopped, apparently because there was an accident or something.
My mother drinks vinegar every morning because she heard it's good for your health.

fields.meaning: A mere…, slightly… (わずかに)
examples: We fell a mere 2 points short of winning the championship.
Only a mere 10 people live in that village now.
A faint light was coming into the room.

fields.meaning: Before long…, eventually… (やがて)
examples: Before long, the rain turned to snow.
Children, too, will eventually become adults.
Before long, spring will come and the flowers will bloom.

fields.meaning: If… (then it's no good: ようでは)
fields.connection: V plain form + ようでは + bad result
examples: If you can't solve a problem this simple, there's no way you'll pass.
If you cry just because you were warned a little, you won't make it in the working world.
If you can't keep your promises, you'll lose people's trust.

fields.meaning: Not… at all (ちっとも～ない)
examples: Even though I took the medicine, I'm not getting any better at all.
His stories aren't interesting at all.
My younger brother doesn't study at all.

fields.meaning: It seems…, apparently… (どうやら)
examples: It looks like it's going to rain tomorrow.
It seems he is serious.
I hear footsteps. It seems someone has come.

fields.meaning: Either way…, in any case… (どうせ)
examples: If we're going to do it anyway, let's have fun doing it.
We won't make it anyway, so let's take the next train.
I had assumed it would be impossible for me anyway.

fields.meaning: At last…, the time has finally come… (いよいよ)
examples: Tomorrow is finally the day of the exam.
Summer vacation is finally starting.
The rain has grown heavier and heavier.

fields.meaning: Not… properly, not… decently (ろくに～ない)
examples: I've been so busy that I haven't slept properly.
He left without even properly saying hello.
Don't complain when you haven't even looked into it properly.

fields.meaning: After going to the trouble of…, a rare chance to… (せっかく)
fields.connection: せっかく + [sentence/clause] ( + のに / のだから)
examples: I went to the trouble of cooking, but nobody ate it.
It's a rare day off, so let's go out somewhere.
Since I'm here in Japan, I'd like to try climbing Mt. Fuji.

fields.meaning: At least…, at the very least… (せめて)
examples: If only I'd had at least one more hour, I would have finished.
Even if you can't do all of it, at least do half.
I wish you had at least sent me a word.

fields.meaning: Long ago, already… a long time ago (とっくに)
examples: The movie started ages ago, you know.
If it's that news, I've known about it for a long time.
He went home a long time ago.

fields.meaning: Very…, much more than usual (よほど/よっぽど)
examples: He must have been really tired, because he fell asleep right away.
This shop is much cheaper.
I seriously thought about saying it, but I held back.

fields.meaning: More and more… (only changing in one direction, usually for the worse)
examples: Prices just keep going up.
The situation is only getting worse.
All we can do is pray that there are no accidents.
There is no solution. All we can do is be patient.
fields.notes:
meaning_vi: (1) more and more
(2)(3) only
used in written language.

fields.meaning: That's what… is, truly… (affirmation of a general feeling)
fields.connection: V plain form/N + というものだ
examples: Reading someone else's letters without permission is an invasion of privacy.
Helping each other in hard times is what friendship is all about.
Making only one person do the work is simply unfair.

fields.meaning: Even though…, despite… (criticism, like くせに)
fields.connection: V/A plain form + くせして / Nの + くせして
examples: Don't pretend to know when you don't.
He's late himself, yet he's strict with others.
Just a child, yet saying such cheeky things.

fields.meaning: All of them…, every one of them…
examples: All three proposals were excellent.
The participants were all young people in their twenties.
Every one of his works is highly regarded.

fields.meaning: However, nevertheless (formal)
examples: The plan is excellent. However, it costs too much.
Many people opposed it. Nevertheless, the construction went ahead.
Technology has advanced. However, new problems are also increasing.

fields.meaning: Slightly, somewhat…
examples: Today is slightly warmer than yesterday.
The price is somewhat on the high side, but the quality is good.
The meeting ran somewhat long.

fields.meaning: There is no choice but to…, have no option but to…
examples: The last train has already left, so I have no choice but to walk home.
It's raining, so we have no choice but to cancel the game.
We don't have the ingredients, so there's no choice but to give up.

fields.meaning: Once… (いったん～たら/ば)
examples: Once you have made a promise, you should be sure to keep it.
Once you start, you can't stop halfway.
Once you have taken something on, take responsibility for it to the end.

fields.meaning: In the unlikely event…, if by any chance…
examples: If by any chance there is a fire, please escape by these stairs.
In an emergency, please call this number.
Even if by some chance you fail, you can just try again.

fields.meaning: From start to finish, everything…
examples: Thank you for everything you have done for me.
He is the complete opposite of me in every way.
My wife took care of every single part of the trip preparations.

fields.meaning: As one wishes… (思うようにいかない)
fields.connection: 思うように + V（usually negative: 思うようにいかない）
examples: My body won't move the way I want it to.
My work isn't progressing as I'd like, and it's frustrating.
Even if you can't speak as well as you'd like, please don't give up.

fields.meaning: Still… even now (has not changed for a long time)
examples: I still can't remember his name.
The cause of the accident is still unknown.
It's been 10 years since I graduated, but I'm still in touch with my teacher.

fields.meaning: Whether you call it… or…
fields.connection: V plain form + というか + V plain form + というか / N + N / Na + Na / Aい + Aい
examples: He's kind, or rather soft, and can't be strict with people.
Surprised, or maybe appalled, I was at a loss for words.
Call it work or call it a hobby, it's fun to do.
Summer in Japan is hot, or rather, muggy.
Today was busy, or rather hectic, so I'm late getting in touch.
His remarks are honest, or maybe rude; listening to him makes me nervous.
fields.explain:
Suited to conversation, blogs and social media; rarely used in formal documents.
Usually pairs two expressions of the same part of speech (N with N, A with A…) to keep the rhythm natural.
Can be used once to correct yourself: A、 というか、B（正確にはB）.
Expresses a modest/softened attitude, avoiding a strong assertion.
The variant っていうか has a more casual nuance.

• Expresses hesitation/rephrasing: “you could say it this way, or you could say it that way”, “or rather…”.
• Usually presents two expressions with similar meanings or two sides of the same thing, showing a vague evaluation that is hard to state definitively.
• Can be used to correct the statement just made: “A… no, more accurately, B”.
• Has a conversational, soft nuance, more narrative/exclamatory than a normative judgment.
fields.notes:
• Put “AというかB” right after the previous statement to adjust it naturally: A（大雑把）→ というかB（精確/婉曲）.
• Don't overuse it with too many long pairs; two phrases at most is most natural.
• In formal presentations, prefer というより/すなわち/つまり, which are clearer than というか.
meaning_vi: I don't know whether to call it ~ or ~
explain: ◎ An expression used when you want to explain something with several different expressions, avoiding asserting it with just one.
examples: 1. この靴は、おしゃれというか、派手というか、デザインが変わっている。
These shoes have an unusual design; I don't know whether to call them stylish or flashy.
2. こういう会は、面倒というか、疲れるというか、あまり行きたくない。
I don't really want to go to gatherings like this; they feel like a hassle, or tiring.
meaning_vi: 思(おも)いつくままに評価(ひょうか)の言葉(ことば)を並(なら)べる
examples: 1. 彼女はかわいいというか子どもっぽいというか、とにかく年よりはずいぶん若く見える。
Whether you call her cute or childish, anyway, she looks much younger than her age.
2. 「父は曲がったことが大嫌いな人です。くそまじめと言うか融通が利かないと言うか・・・・・」
My father is someone who hates anything crooked. He's extremely serious, and also inflexible.
3. 「山本のやつ、会社を辞めて自転車で世界一周旅行をするんだって。勇気があると言うか無謀と言うか。でも、ちょっとうらやましいなあ」
That guy Yamamoto, I hear he's quitting his job to travel around the world by bicycle. He's brave and reckless at the same time. Still, I'm a bit jealous!
mistakes: Mixing parts of speech: A is a noun and B is a verb, which sounds forced. Keep the same part of speech when possible.
Using it in formal documents (reports, theses) makes them less serious; the JLPT often sets traps with a formal context → choose というより/すなわち.
Confusing it with というより: if the sentence needs to “negate A to choose B”, you must use というより, not というか.
Repeating というか too many times in one sentence makes it wordy and incoherent.
JLPT level: というか usually appears at N2 (also seen at N3 in conversational contexts); questions often test the nuance of “adjusting what was said”.

fields.meaning: On the way (out/back)… (行きがけに)
examples: Pick up some milk on your way home.
On my way there, I stopped by the post office.
Just as I was about to leave, the phone rang, and I ended up being late.

fields.meaning: Not… (classical modifier: 見えざる敵)
fields.connection: Vない (drop ない) + ざる + N / する → せざる
examples: He was fighting an invisible enemy.
He was an uninvited guest.
This town has a hidden history.
